reasons: Claimed status is compliant with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output shape; the rendered redline is identical to the original paragraphs, so nothing improper was inserted.

The cited text (§ 11.3, p0132–p0137) is a breach-investigation and remedy provision tied to the § 11.2(b) content warranties; it grants no access to Customer premises, systems, personnel, books or records, and imposes no audit cost or cooperation burden, so there is no audit right to parametrize.

Absence of any audit right binding Customer is better than the AUDIT preferred position and benefits our party; flagging it as 'missing' and inserting frequency/notice/cost limits would manufacture a verification right in IBM's favour, contrary to the rule's purpose and the no-flagging-favourable-terms instruction.

The failing 'audit frequency limited' deterministic check is correctly explained as an artifact of absence rather than a material failure; no walk-away trigger (unlimited/unannounced audits or remote access to Customer systems) is present because no audit or access right is granted.
The residual observation about § 11.3's best-efforts notice is appropriately noted in the rationale rather than escalated, consistent with the minor sub-element handling rule.
